core.title: Give every wagon produce/consume entry a version-free contract URN that resolves in the registry
core.given: A wagon manifest (a plan artifact) declares produce/consume entries that name artifacts by domain, resource and an optional category facet, backed by the contract registry.
core.when: You author or edit those entries, roll contract URNs out across wagons, or change registry contract ids or producers.
core.then: Every produce/consume entry in a wagon manifest carries a version-free contract URN — the profile's contract-URN shape applied to the entry's artifact name, unchanged — that resolves to a contract in the registry (any version) whose producer names the producing wagon.
prefer: Derive the URN from the artifact name per the profile's contract-URN shape: domain first, then resource, with the optional category facet preserved; the name is otherwise unchanged.
Same URN on the producer's produce entry and every consume entry; each consume entry names the producing wagon through the profile's consume producer-reference idiom.
Upgrade in order: add urn to all wagon artifacts; validate all resolve; generate missing contracts for orphaned URNs.
avoid: Legacy URNs that use the facet separator for domain/resource hierarchy; migrate them to the profile's contract-URN shape.
Versions or schema/API detail in the URN.
Changing URNs when a contract moves to a new version.
Dropping the category facet when deriving the URN from the artifact name.
unless: Pre-URN wagons: the urn field is optional initially; it is required for new wagons.
core.why: Wagons declare WHAT (URN), contracts HOW (version, schema, API): contracts evolve without wagon-manifest changes, names stay readable, and the graph keeps bidirectional wagon<->contract linkage.
evidence: Every produce/consume entry in a wagon manifest has a urn matching the profile's contract-URN shape and equal to the contract prefix plus the entry's artifact name, unchanged.
Each URN resolves to a contract in the contract registry: some versioned contract id matching the URN body, at any version.
The matched contract's producer resolves back to the wagon whose produce entry carries the URN (bidirectional linkage).
verification: Shape check: every produce/consume entry's urn matches the profile's contract-URN shape and equals the contract prefix plus the entry's artifact name unchanged (domain, resource and any category facet all preserved).

Resolution check: each URN resolves to a contract in the contract registry — some versioned contract id whose body matches the URN, at any version; the registry id is the authoritative source for schema, version and API.

Linkage check: the matched contract's producer resolves back to the wagon whose produce entry carries the URN (bidirectional wagon<->contract linkage); an unresolved URN or a broken back-link is a finding.
Legacy normalisation: a URN that uses the facet separator for hierarchy normalises to the profile's contract-URN shape, with the category kept as a facet, and is migrated rather than left in place.
Backward compatibility: a missing urn on a pre-existing (pre-rollout) wagon manifest is tolerated initially; a missing urn on a new wagon manifest is a finding.
The rollout is checked in order: urn added to all wagon artifacts, then all URNs validated to resolve, then missing contracts generated for orphaned URNs.
Out of scope: a version-only registry bump (no artifact rename, no producer change) — the URN is unchanged by design.

values: registry contract id or producer field added/changed/removed

fires: Planner adds a produce entry to a new wagon manifest
Planner adds a consume entry referencing an artifact produced by another wagon
Planner edits an existing urn field or renames a produced/consumed artifact
Planner meets a legacy URN in a manifest that uses the facet separator for hierarchy and must migrate it
Planner runs the URN rollout: adding urn to all wagon artifacts, validating resolution, and generating contracts for orphaned URNs
Planner changes a contract id or producer field in the registry so a wagon URN may no longer resolve or link back
A wagon-manifest edit or a registry edit alone activates (the two are alternatives); an ordinary manifest edit does not also require touching the registry
doesNotFire: Editing prose docs or acceptances that do not touch wagon-manifest produce/consume entries or registry ids/producers
Bumping a contract version in the registry without renaming the artifact or changing its producer (the URN stays unchanged)
Code-only changes outside the plan root and the contract registry

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (version-free contract URN derived from the artifact name, registry resolution at any version, producer back-link, ordered rollout, pre-URN tolerance) is stack-neutral. All concrete shapes, locations and idioms are profile data: manifest location/kind (roles.plan_artifact.path/kinds), the registry location (layout.registries#contracts, proposed), the URN and registry-id shapes (urn.contract / urn.grammar#contract_id, proposed — the vocabulary's urn group has no contract kind), and the consume-entry producer-reference syntax (idiom.plan_syntax#consume_producer_reference, proposed — the idiom group has no manifest producer-reference key); another stack supplies its own corresponding syntax for the core's 'consume entries name the producing wagon'. Bun's path_glob activation fact became a file_kind fact because the neutral fact vocabulary has no path fact; its OR note ('either side alone activates') moved into fires. Worked examples with real wagon names (including the concrete `from wagon:maintain-ux` instance) and the literal check regex stay Bun-side; bun.json is delivered as the reference example. 'Wagon' is retained as neutral vocabulary (the profile vocabulary itself defines wagons as bounded product slices), and 'registry'/'manifest' name convention concepts, not stack mechanisms.
